questionText:

(A) India joined the UN
(B) Tehran Conference Declaration of the Three Powers (US, Britain and Soviet Union)
(C) Signing of the Atlantic Charter by the US President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British PM Winston S. Churchill
(D) The UN was founded

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 6: International Organisations, 'Declaration and Evolution of the UN' timeline, p. 83): (C) Signing of the Atlantic Charter by FDR and Churchill took place in August 1941. (B) Declaration of the Three Powers at the Tehran Conference occurred in December 1943. (D) The United Nations was officially founded on 24 October 1945 when the Charter was ratified. (A) India joined the UN as an original founding member on 30 October 1945. Chronological sequence: (C) [1941] -> (B) [1943] -> (D) [24 Oct 1945] -> (A) [30 Oct 1945].
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct about elections in India?
(A) The Congress Party won more seats in the Lok Sabha in 1989 elections than in 1984 elections.
(B) The 1991 Lok Sabha elections marked the end of the 'Congress system'.
(C) The Lok Sabha elections in 1989 led to the defeat of the Congress party but did not result in a majority for any other party.
(D) In 1989 the National Front formed a coalition government at the centre.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Recent Developments in Indian Politics.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Recent Developments in Indian Politics (Crises of the Constitutional Order):
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 9: Recent Developments in Indian Politics, 'Era of Coalitions'): (A) In 1984 Congress won an unprecedented 415 seats, whereas in 1989 it won only 197 seats; hence statement (A) is false. (B) The 1989 (not 1991) election marked the end of what political scientists called the 'Congress system' (Statement B is false). (C) Congress was defeated in 1989, but no other party secured a majority of its own (Statement C is correct). (D) The National Front (an alliance of Janata Dal and regional parties) formed a government led by V.P. Singh with outside support from BJP and Left Front (Statement D is correct). Thus (C) and (D) only are correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I
List-II
(A) Gujarat Movement
(IV) January 1974
(B) Bihar Movement
(III) March 1974
(C) Assam Movement
(II) 1979
(D) Railway Strike
(I) May 1974
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for The Crisis of Democratic Order.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For The Crisis of Democratic Order (Crises of the Constitutional Order):
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 6 & Chapter 8): (A) Gujarat student movement against price rise and corruption began in January 1974 (IV). (B) Bihar student movement led by Jayaprakash Narayan began in March 1974 (III). (C) Assam movement led by AASU against illegal migration started in 1979 (II). (D) Nationwide Railway Strike led by George Fernandes was called in May 1974 (I). Matching: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
